title: Glock wins Red Bull Ring Race 2 as Ekström takes second on strategy
dek: Timo Glock passed pole-sitter Jamie Green on lap two and won DTM Race 2 for BMW Team RMG, with Ekström up from 11th to second and Mercedes failing to score.

chapters.title: BMW wins on Saturday, Mercedes searches for answers
text: Saturday had gone BMW's way. Marco Wittmann won Race 1 from pole for Team RMG, Tom Blomqvist made it a one-two, and six M4 DTMs finished in the top ten while Edoardo Mortara's Audi was the only car to split the BMWs on the podium. Mercedes had managed only a seventh place, from Paul di Resta, who nevertheless left the opening day as the championship leader on 43 points, three ahead of Mortara, with Wittmann third on 29.

Sunday's race was set at 60 minutes plus one lap and carried a mandatory pit stop for a tyre change, so strategy would count for more. With the sun out and temperatures climbing, the question was how the new asphalt, which had produced so much grip on Saturday, would behave in the heat.

chapters.title: Green takes pole by two thousandths
text: Audi, who had struggled in Saturday's qualifying and race, were much more competitive on Sunday morning. Jamie Green went second-fastest early on, 0.084 seconds behind António Félix da Costa, then found more on his second set of tyres and took pole for Team Rosberg with a 1m22.680s, a margin of just 0.002 seconds over the Schnitzer BMW.

BMW still filled much of the top of the order. Timo Glock was third and Maxime Martin fourth, with Mortara fifth and Augusto Farfus sixth on an identical 1m22.812s, followed by Bruno Spengler, Blomqvist and Mike Rockenfeller. Wittmann, the Saturday winner, qualified tenth, 0.203 seconds off pole. Mattias Ekström managed only 11th.

It was another bad session for Mercedes. Robert Wickens was the best of them in 15th, 0.378 seconds off the pace, and di Resta, the championship leader, was slowest of all 24 cars, 0.640 seconds behind Green. The grid was not exactly the qualifying order: on the grid di Resta lined up 22nd, with Martin Tomczyk 23rd and Esteban Ocon last.

chapters.title: Glock takes the lead, a safety car follows
text: Green and Félix da Costa got slightly better getaways than the rest, but when Félix da Costa challenged Green into the first corner he ran wide over the kerbs and lost momentum. Glock, who had started third, took second from him at Remus and then closed on Green. On lap two he used the DRS to get past the Audi at Turn 2 and into the lead.

Further back, Wickens tried to pass Nico Müller at Würth Kurve and tagged the Audi, sending it across the gravel and into the barriers, and the safety car came out for three laps. Glock timed the restart well and pulled away at once from Green, who was again under pressure from Félix da Costa. The Portuguese could not find a way through and was passed by Mortara, Farfus and Martin in the following corners. Glock's lead soon stretched to about two seconds.

chapters.title: Ekström stays out and Mortara meets Félix da Costa
text: The mandatory stops began in the middle of the race. Glock was one of the first to come in, on lap 15, and returned in clear air. Green stopped a few laps later and could not make up the gap. Ekström had a different plan: he stayed out as long as he could and made good times on his old tyres.

The battle for fourth turned the race around. Félix da Costa, who had climbed back by stopping early, passed Mortara after Schlosshold and tried to close the door into Rauch; Mortara tagged the rear of the BMW and both cars ended in the gravel. Félix da Costa rejoined and finished 21st, while Mortara lost a great deal of time and was classified 23rd, 18 laps down. Ekström came in on lap 28 and rejoined third, ahead of Farfus, on fresher tyres and with more grip than before, he said.

chapters.title: Glock wins comfortably, Ekström passes Green
text: Ekström closed on his fellow Audi driver Green, who gave up second place without a fight when it became clear the Swede was faster. Ekström then tried to reel in Glock but the win was out of reach: after 41 laps Glock crossed the line 2.976 seconds ahead, with Green a further 3.279 seconds back in third.

Farfus was fourth, ahead of Martin, Blomqvist and Wittmann, so that BMW took the next four places behind the Audis. Rockenfeller, Spengler and Timo Scheider completed the top ten. Scheider defended the final point against Gary Paffett on the last lap, and Paffett was forced out wide onto the grass. His 11th was still the best finish for a Mercedes. Wickens, 20th after the earlier contact, set the fastest lap of the race on lap 40, a 1m23.446s.

chapters.title: Glock climbs the table as Mercedes goes pointless
text: The win was Glock's third in the DTM and his first of 2016, and it completed a weekend in which Team RMG took both races, Wittmann winning on Saturday and Glock on Sunday. Glock said afterwards that the Hankook tyres had been outstanding and that tyre management had been easy, in part because the circuit was unusually free of bumps. The result lifted him to 37 points in the championship, level with Martin and six behind the leader. BMW placed five cars in the top seven, and Wittmann's seventh place added six points to his Saturday win, so that both Team RMG drivers left Austria well placed in the table.

Behind Glock, both Audi drivers were happy with the podium. Ekström, who started from 11th, thanked his team and said the grip had actually increased when he rejoined after his stop and that this allowed him to pass Green. Green, who had been on pole, said the new surface and the high temperatures had made the afternoon tricky, but his third place gave him his first points of the season, after three races without a point.

Mercedes left Austria with nothing from the second race, whose best finisher was Paffett in 11th. Di Resta finished 15th after starting 22nd, yet he still led the championship on 43 points, just three ahead of Mortara, who scored nothing after the contact with Félix da Costa and stayed on 40. Martin and Glock were next on 37, with Wittmann on 35 and Blomqvist on 34, so six drivers were within nine points of the lead. Among those who finished without points, Wickens was 20th after his drive in the incident with Müller, and Müller, who completed only one lap, was last.

The next round is at the Lausitzring on 3 to 5 June. The 2016 season has 18 races over nine weekends, so 14 are still to come and the championship is wide open. Hankook's tyre engineers noted that the Ventus Race tyres had shown no signs of wear on the new surface, even with the track around ten degrees hotter than on Saturday, and drivers from all three manufacturers said the grip had been high from start to finish.

facts.v: Glock took the lead on lap two and won for the third time in the DTM, his first success of the 2016 season.
